title: Personal Loans Servicing Standard: Loans Under Hardship Plans and Payment Protection
content:
## Standard

Holding a Hardship Assistance Programs plan or a Payment Protection benefit changes how a Personal Loans loan is serviced. When a hardship plan on the loan becomes active, the loan's current interest rate, installment amount, next due date and maturity date are set to the plan's terms; deferred installments move the next due date and the maturity date forward by one month each. When a temporary plan (Short-Term Payment Deferral, Reduced Payment Plan, Temporary Rate Reduction Plan, Disaster Relief Deferral, Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit) ends for any reason, the rate returns to the base interest rate minus the AutoPay discount if AutoPay is active and the installment returns to its pre-plan amount, while the moved maturity date stays; a Term Extension Modification is permanent. Payments credited toward a plan installment count as installments paid on time when the plan installment is paid in full. While a hardship plan on the loan is in requested, offered or active status, the loan cannot be refinanced and its due day cannot be changed.

A Payment Protection benefit paid to the loan posts as a payment of type protection benefit and is applied like any other payment. When a Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit is applied, the interest paid since the military service start date above the capped rate is credited to principal as one interest credit (servicemember benefit); interest charged because of a Larkspur error is credited the same way (lender error). An interest credit never pays out cash. A plan that sets its own rate (a plan interest rate on the plan) replaces the AutoPay-discounted rate while it is active; a plan that does not set a rate leaves the AutoPay-discounted rate in place.

## Temporary and permanent programs

| Program | When it ends |
|---|---|
| Short-Term Payment Deferral, Reduced Payment Plan, Temporary Rate Reduction Plan, Disaster Relief Deferral, Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit | rate and installment return as stated above; the moved maturity date stays |
| Term Extension Modification | permanent |

## Cases (hypothetical)

- A loan on AutoPay enters a plan with no plan rate: the AutoPay-discounted rate stays in place during the plan.
- A loan on AutoPay enters a plan with its own plan rate: the plan rate replaces the discounted rate while the plan is active; when a temporary plan ends with AutoPay still on, the rate is the base interest rate minus the AutoPay discount.
- A loan with a hardship plan in offered status: a refinance or a due-day change is not available until no plan is requested, offered or active.
